components.name: marginal_outcomes
components.source_to_target_assumptions: Same-population A0 reconstruction. Lognormal weight; beta-distributed PFS on [1,5] rounded to 1/15; negative-binomial integer gng on [0,512]; beta dd100 and dd1000 on [0,1]. Distributional shapes are assumptions. Beta and negative-binomial parameters match source population-style moments; randomized finite cohorts need not match exactly. Weight is truncated at 180 kg only at baseline. Truncation and PFS rounding slightly alter fitted moments.

components.name: conditional_quantile_sampling
components.source_to_target_assumptions: At each observed visit/outcome margin, sample one uniform value per equal-probability stratum and assign quantiles by stochastic Gaussian latent ranks. This produces stochastic cohorts conditional on supplied marginals with less finite-cohort marginal variability than iid sampling. It does not reproduce individual rows and does not provide a sampling-uncertainty model.

components.name: longitudinal_and_cross_endpoint_dependence
components.source_to_target_assumptions: All scenarios use parent latent persistent variance fractions weight=0.85, pfs=0.60, gng=0.45, dd100=0.60, dd1000=0.60. Target retains independent endpoints. Shared_trait correlates person intercepts using one standard normal factor. Shared_state correlates visit innovations using one independent standard normal factor per person/visit. Signed factor loadings in endpoint order are [0.65,0.70,0.65,-0.75,-0.75]. Each correlated component is loading*common+sqrt(1-loading^2)*independent, so positive semidefiniteness and unit component variances follow by construction. These loadings and persistence values are explicit sensitivity choices, not estimated quantities, exact observed-scale correlations, or empirical directional claims. Marginal rank assignment and masking alter observed-scale dependence.

components.name: missingness
components.source_to_target_assumptions: Exact visit/outcome observed counts at n=75; int(round(n_observed*n/75)) at other n. Rank availability scores composed of independent normal person (variance 0.50), shared person-visit (0.30), and endpoint-visit (0.20) components. The overlap and persistent absence are assumed; no monotone dropout is enforced. Scores are independent of all outcome latent variables, giving a conditional-count MCAR mechanism. Source individual masks and informative missingness are unknown.

components.name: synthetic_identity
components.source_to_target_assumptions: New numeric person IDs 1 through n; every person has one row at each declared visit. Local default_rng(seed), no file or network I/O, and no evidence mutation.

scenarios.assumption: A persistent person-level factor makes weight, PFS and No-Go ranks covary positively and discounting AUC ranks covary in the opposite direction; both discounting conditions share the same sign. Shared residual innovations are absent.
scenarios.inclusion_rationale: A stable common individual propensity is an evidence-compatible explanation of cross-outcome dependence that the independent parent excludes. It produces cross-endpoint, cross-visit covariance and can materially affect standardized associations and random-intercept trajectory uncertainty. The loading signs are hypotheses solely for sensitivity.

scenarios.assumption: A shared person-visit state with the same signed loadings links concurrent measurements; endpoint-specific person intercepts remain independent. State shocks are independent across visits.
scenarios.inclusion_rationale: Transient context or measurement-session effects are an evidence-compatible alternative to a stable common trait. Concurrent associations may be present while cross-endpoint cross-visit covariance is absent at the latent level. This changes what repeated-measure associations mean without introducing an unsupported marginal trend.
